idiom_name: JSX props passed through function components
implementation_notes: Props are ordinary object properties and JSX wires them into the component tree, so the explicit relay needs no library: React's documentation calls passing props a great way to explicitly pipe data through the UI tree and names the deep case 'prop drilling'. The discipline that keeps it healthy is to keep state at the least common ancestor of its consumers (lifting state up), avoid splitting components into extra layers before reuse demands it, and inline relay components or replace them with `{children}` composition so they stop declaring props they never read.
pitfalls: Optional or defaulted props hide a missing relay: a value that consumers require should be required in the props object (and checked by the linter/types).
Adding a layer only to forward props is the common cause: prefer `{children}` and element props so the value never enters the intermediate's API.

variants.name: React Context API (provider + useContext)
variants.implementation_notes: React's Context API is the framework-provided replacement: `createContext` creates the key, a provider supplies the value to the subtree below it, and any descendant reads it with `useContext` - no intermediate props. It pays off when a value is needed by many distant leaves (theme, locale, current user) and is unnecessary for one or two levels, where explicit props stay more traceable. Keep the provider scope as narrow as the consumers' common ancestor and memoise the value, because every consumer re-renders when the provider's value changes.
pitfalls: A context object imported through two module copies (duplicate packages, symlinks, separate bundles) is not the same context: provider and consumer identity is compared with `===`.
Passing a fresh object literal as the provider value re-renders every consumer on every render of the provider; memoise the value.

variants.name: Vue provide/inject or Svelte context
variants.idiom_name: Vue 3 provide()/inject() or Svelte createContext set/get
variants.implementation_notes: Vue's documentation titles the problem 'Prop Drilling' and answers it with provide/inject: a parent becomes the dependency provider and any descendant injects the value, bypassing intermediates - the page notes that a component which 'may not care about these props at all' still had to declare and pass them. Svelte offers the same idea through `createContext` (a `[get, set, has]` triplet) with an ownership check. Both mechanisms are framework-level, scoped to the component instance tree rather than to a module.
pitfalls: provide/inject is not reactive state management: injecting a raw value loses reactivity in Vue unless the provided value is a ref/reactive object.
Svelte's `createContext` must be called inside component initialisation, not lazily in a helper, or the owner check fails.
